description: Reasoning vault aligned with OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §4.2: build original linear models from verbal descriptions and pairs of input-output data, then interpret and use their predictions within a meaningful domain.

archetypes.name: Build a Model from a Starting Value and Rate
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §4.2 — Building Linear Models from Verbal Descriptions
archetypes.coreConcept: A constant rate and an initial amount determine a linear rule for a changing quantity.
archetypes.mentalModel: Start at the initial amount, then add the same rate-sized change for every input unit elapsed.

cognitiveTraps.description: Interchanging the starting amount and per-unit rate when building a model.
Using a positive rate for a quantity that consistently decreases, or a negative rate for one that increases.
Using a rate whose units do not match the chosen input unit.
cognitiveTraps.trapFormula: per hour ↦ multiply by minutes without conversion

usedContexts: A reserve tank contains a starting amount of water, and a pump adds water at a steady rate.

figureBuilders.title: A starting quantity changes at a constant rate

archetypes.name: Build a Model from Two Observations
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §4.2 — Using Given Input and Output Values to Build a Model
archetypes.coreConcept: Two observations with distinct inputs determine the constant rate and the line that models the relationship.
archetypes.mentalModel: Compare paired changes to find the rate, anchor the line at one observation, and check it against the other.

cognitiveTraps.description: Pairing an input value with the output from a different observation.
Using only the rate and omitting the nonzero initial amount or intercept.

usedContexts: A workshop production dashboard tracks a running total that includes orders completed before the monitoring window; additional orders are completed at a constant pace.

labels.label: A linear model from paired observations

figureBuilders.title: Two observations determine a constant-rate model

archetypes.name: Predict a Quantity from a Linear Model
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §4.2 — Using a Linear Model to Make a Prediction
archetypes.coreConcept: Evaluating a contextual linear function gives the modeled output for a stated input.
archetypes.mentalModel: Translate the question's input into the model, evaluate, and preserve the quantity's units and meaning.

cognitiveTraps.description: Multiplying the starting quantity by elapsed time while adding the rate once.
Substituting an input measured in a different time unit without converting it.

usedContexts: A packing station's queue monitor tracks the number of boxes waiting as a function of minutes after a shift begins.
archetypes.figureNone: The task evaluates a stated rule at one input; a figure adds no information needed for the calculation.

archetypes.name: Interpret Intercepts and Find a Target Input
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §4.2 — Interpreting Linear Model Intercepts
archetypes.coreConcept: The vertical intercept represents the modeled starting output, while a horizontal intercept identifies when the modeled output reaches zero; solving for a target output reverses the model.
archetypes.mentalModel: Translate a target quantity into an equation, solve for the input, then test whether that input fits the situation's time or quantity domain.

cognitiveTraps.description: Evaluating the model at the target output instead of solving for the input that produces it.
Reporting a predicted input outside the stated period or beyond a physical stopping condition.
Treating a consumption rate as positive when solving for elapsed time to a lower target quantity.

usedContexts: A small reservoir supplies a steady-use system; its water level is tracked by volume over time.

figureBuilders.title: A decreasing balance reaches a target value
